summary: The reader has completed an undergraduate computer science degree: big-O analysis, polynomials and complex numbers, and Turing machines with tapes, plus the discrete mathematics and first linear algebra course that such a degree requires. For the paper this means modular arithmetic, gcd and primes, roots of unity, binary arithmetic over F2 with Hamming weight, and basic vector-space and matrix facts (subspaces, rank, projections, dot product, eigenvalues) at first-course depth. Bilinear forms, tensor products, finite-field and ring theory, the Chinese remainder theorem, Newton iteration and the Fourier and convolution machinery beyond the basics are treated as not known.

known.name: Mathematical induction
known.gloss: A proof method that establishes a statement for all natural numbers by proving a base case and that each case implies the next.

known.name: Logarithms and floor and ceiling functions
known.gloss: The logarithm inverts exponentiation, and the floor and ceiling functions round a real number down or up to an integer.

known.name: Binary representation of integers
known.gloss: Every nonnegative integer has a unique representation as a finite sum of powers of two with coefficients 0 or 1, written as a string of bits.

known.name: Dyadic rationals
known.gloss: Rational numbers whose denominator is a power of two, equivalently those with a finite binary expansion.

known.name: Modular arithmetic
known.gloss: Integers a and b are congruent modulo m when m divides their difference, and arithmetic is carried out on remainders after division by m.

known.name: Greatest common divisor and coprimality
known.gloss: The greatest common divisor of two integers is the largest integer dividing both, computed by the Euclidean algorithm, and two integers are coprime when their gcd is 1.

known.name: Prime numbers
known.gloss: A prime is an integer greater than 1 whose only positive divisors are 1 and itself, and every integer greater than 1 factors uniquely into primes.

known.name: Roots of unity
aliases: powers of a root of unity
known.gloss: A complex number z is an n-th root of unity when z^n = 1, and a primitive n-th root of unity is one whose successive powers give all n of the n-th roots.

known.name: Binary field F2 and XOR arithmetic
known.gloss: The integers modulo 2, with addition given by exclusive or and multiplication by logical AND, in which each element is its own additive inverse.

known.name: Hamming weight
known.gloss: The Hamming weight of a binary string is the number of positions that hold a 1.

known.name: Vector spaces and subspaces
known.gloss: A vector space is a set closed under addition and scalar multiplication, and a subspace is a subset that is itself a vector space; a basis is a linearly independent spanning set and the dimension is the size of any basis.

known.name: Matrices and linear maps
known.gloss: A matrix represents a linear map between finite-dimensional vector spaces, and matrices multiply, invert and transpose in the standard way.

known.name: Matrix rank
known.gloss: The rank of a matrix is the dimension of its column space, which equals the maximum number of linearly independent columns.

known.name: Projection onto a subspace
known.gloss: A projection is a linear map P with P squared equal to P, which fixes its image pointwise and maps onto a chosen subspace.

known.name: Dot product and orthogonality
known.gloss: The dot product of two vectors is the sum of the products of their corresponding coordinates, and two vectors are orthogonal when their dot product is zero.

known.name: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
known.gloss: A scalar lambda is an eigenvalue of a square matrix A when some nonzero vector v satisfies Av = lambda v, and such a v is an eigenvector.
